guide.summary: Harvest time tracking, public OAuth2 app (self-serve, wait none); Greenhouse Harvest API (recruiting) (partner acceptance).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Harvest time tracking, public OAuth2 app (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Greenhouse Harvest API (recruiting) (partner acceptance).

composio.note: Composio lists Harvest as managed OAuth. The dossier does not say whether the toolkit targets Harvest time tracking or Greenhouse Harvest; confirm on the toolkit page.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed Harvest app. For launch, bring your own app if users should see your brand, you want dedicated quota, or you need shorter trigger polling.
reasons: Managed consent screen shows Composio's name, not yours
Managed app quota is shared across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval
Own app recommended where the consent screen must show your brand

scenarios.label: Harvest time tracking, public OAuth2 app
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your users use Harvest (getharvest.com) and you register an OAuth2 app in Harvest ID.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: The docs describe no provider review step (c2). Not explicitly confirmed as review-free.

scenarios.approval: No review is described in the docs; the path is inferred from the registration docs.

scenarios.label: Greenhouse Harvest API (recruiting)
scenarios.when_this_applies: You actually mean Greenhouse's Harvest API and need partner OAuth for many customers.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: No verified source backs this timeline (the agent's estimate was "About 1-3 months (provider advises planning in months)").

scenarios.approval: Needs a signed Greenhouse partnership agreement. Applications are reviewed monthly, and not all are accepted.

prerequisites.title: Confirm which Harvest you mean
prerequisites.detail: The dossier mixes Harvest time tracking with Greenhouse's Harvest API; they have different approval paths.

prerequisites.title: Harvest ID account with Developers access
prerequisites.detail: Create the OAuth2 app from the Developers section of Harvest ID. Older V1 docs say registering requires an Administrator.

prerequisites.title: Mutual customer, website and privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Partner acceptance requires at least one mutual customer and an active website with a privacy policy.

steps.title: Decide which Harvest product you target
steps.detail: Confirm whether users are on Harvest time tracking or Greenhouse recruiting. This picks the scenario.

steps.title: Register OAuth2 app in Harvest ID
steps.detail: In the Developers section, enter name, redirect URL, multi-account setting and products.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret are shown

steps.title: Pick minimal products and scopes
steps.detail: Draft the product choice (Harvest, Forecast or both) with the least access that works.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the Harvest app.

steps.title: Submit integration request form
steps.detail: Fill out Greenhouse's integration request form to start the partnership.

steps.title: Wait for monthly Greenhouse review
steps.detail: Applications are reviewed on the first Monday of each month, with a response about 7 business days later. An urgent case with a named mutual customer can ask for an out-of-cycle review.

steps.title: Email credential request to Partner Support
steps.detail: Send integration name, environment, full scope list, every final redirect URI and a 128x128 logo.

steps.title: Draft scope list and redirect URIs
steps.detail: Prepare the complete scope list up front, since later changes need another email.

traps.title: On the V1 OAuth 2.0 page, each user's access
traps.detail: On the V1 OAuth 2.0 page, each user's access token expires in 18 hours (the page does not mention a testing-mode difference).

traps.title: Two different products named Harvest
traps.detail: Evidence for Greenhouse's partner process does not apply to Harvest time tracking, and the reverse. Which one the Composio toolkit uses is unconfirmed.

traps.title: Scope and redirect changes cost an email and a wait
traps.detail: Partners cannot edit scopes or redirect URIs themselves. Adding a scope also forces every customer to re-authorize.

traps.title: Idle Greenhouse connections die
traps.detail: Refresh tokens last 14 days and rotate on every refresh. An idle connection dies at day 15.

traps.title: Non-admin authorizers get 403s
traps.detail: Correct scopes are not enough; a non-admin authorizing user gets 403 on effectively every read.

traps.title: Managed app is branded Composio
traps.detail: Users see Composio's name on consent, and quota is shared with other Composio users.

traps.title: V1 docs are legacy
traps.detail: The V1 OAuth pages describe a deprecated API with an 18-hour token expiry; use the V2 docs.

blockers.symptom: Greenhouse partner application is refused or delayed
blockers.what_it_means: Not every application is accepted, and reviews run once a month.
blockers.what_to_do: Use customer-created credentials in the meantime, or ask for an out-of-cycle review with a named mutual customer.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the request form answers and the customer credential instructions.

blockers.symptom: Customer cannot see the Dev Center option
blockers.what_it_means: Their user lacks permission to manage all organization API credentials.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask a Site Admin or a user with that permission to set up the connection.

open_questions: Does Harvest time tracking run any provider review for apps used by other accounts? Docs found show none; confirm with Harvest support.
Does the Composio 'harvest' toolkit target Harvest time tracking or Greenhouse Harvest? Check the toolkit page at docs.composio.dev/toolkits/harvest.
Is there an unmanaged-app limit (users or rate limit) for Harvest time tracking OAuth apps? Not found; ask Harvest support or test.
What exactly does the Greenhouse review check, and what triggers it beyond 'always'? Ask partneronboarding@greenhouse.io.
Not found: what each review or verification checks and what the developer must submit. Checked getharvest.com, github.com.

evidence.answer: Not every marketplace integration uses Harvest v3, so the directory is not evidence of what a partner is built on.

items.reason: The quote states that building integrations other users can use requires registering an OAuth2 Application.
The quote confirms the URL lets users authenticate on Harvest ID and authorize account access. No review step appears in the quotes, which is consistent with the statement.
The quote says it is advised to pick the minimal scope.
The quote states the products option sets the scope of access as Harvest, Forecast or both.
The quote says the default Redirect URL can be customized, but it does not mention the requirement that the redirect_uri start with the registered URL.
The quote says the user chooses which account to authorize. The condition 'registered for only one account' does not appear in the quote.
The quote states Greenhouse reviews applications on the first Monday of every month and then shares an API agreement.
The quote says a mutual customer is 'required', not 'helpful'.
The quote states an active website with a privacy policy is also required.
The quote states not every application is accepted.
The quote supports Partner Portal and sandbox, then build-and-submit-for-review, then directory. It is truncated and does not mention co-marketing.
The quote states there is no portal, no console, and no way to self-register a client ID.
The quote supports a response within about 7 business days of the review. The advice to plan in months rather than days is not in the quotes.
The quote states testing is for your own sandbox only and production is live for mutual customers.
The quote says a platform can run this way by having each customer generate a pair and paste it in.
The quote states only a Site Admin can pick the option.
The quote states refresh tokens last 14 days, are rotated on every refresh, and an idle connection dies at day 15.
The quote says existing tokens stay valid but never gain the new permission. It is truncated and does not state that every customer must re-authorize.
The quote states a connector with perfect scopes and a non-admin authorizer will 403 on effectively every read.
The quote states Harvest v3 is available for the new subscription tiers Core, Plus, and Pro.
The quote supports that a customer can request an out-of-cycle review by email to partneronboarding. The 'urgent' and 'named mutual customer' conditions are not in the quote.
The quotes describe a self-serve path (create the app in Developers, authorize via Harvest ID) with no provider review mentioned.
The quotes support registering the OAuth2 app in Developers. Copying the client ID and secret is not mentioned.
The quotes require a signed partnership agreement, a monthly Greenhouse review, and state there is no self-registration of a client ID.
The quotes state a signed partnership agreement is required to get started and that applications are reviewed monthly, with no self-registration route.
The quotes support the partnership agreement, monthly review, and API agreement. The request form, emailing Partner Support for credentials, and build-and-submit steps are not in the quotes.
The quotes do not describe what the review checks.
The quote says a response comes within about 7 business days of the review, which conflicts with a 1-3 month wait.
The quote says a platform can run by having each customer generate and paste a credential pair. It does not say this skips the partnership.
The quotes state credential management requires Basic and above, and only a Site Admin can pick the service-account option.
The quote states testing credentials are for your own sandbox only.
The quote states a mutual customer is required.
The quote states Harvest v3 partner integrations are available for Core, Plus, and Pro tiers.
The quotes support no stated review for the Harvest path and the monthly review plus 7-business-day response for Greenhouse. The 'about an hour' estimate is not in the quotes.
